title: Canonical integral cohomological factors
statement: Let $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ be a smooth-proper datum over the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, and fix an indeterminate $T$. For every prime $\ell\neq p$ let $P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\Ql))\in\Ql[T]$, $0\leq i\leq2d$, be the determinant factors of the smooth-proper cohomological family of $\mathscr X$, and for $P=\sum_rc_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$ write $P^{(\ell)}=(\mathbf Z[T]\to\Ql[T])(P)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$ for its coefficientwise extension. By [prop-integral-recovery] there is exactly one tuple $(P_0,\ldots,P_{2d})\in\mathbf Z[T]^{2d+1}$ such that, for every $0\leq i\leq2d$, $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}$ for every prime $\ell\neq p$; each $P_i$ is an integral realization-independent factor in degree $i$ in the sense of [def-weil-integral-frobenius-factor], normalized by $P_i(0)=1$. The *canonical integral cohomological factor* of $\mathscr X$ in degree $i$ is the $i$-th member of this tuple, written $P_i(\mathscr X)$, or simply $P_i$ once $\mathscr X$ is fixed; thus $P_i(\mathscr X)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ and $P_i(\mathscr X)(0)=1$. The tuple depends only on $\mathscr X$: it involves no choice of an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q$ or of an embedding comparing algebraic numbers with $\ell$-adic numbers.
